selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is this passage mainly trying to explain?
questions.answer: It is explaining a deep proof of Allah’s oneness and how Allah can create great and small things with the same ease.

questions.question: Why is this idea described as a mystery or riddle?
questions.answer: Because it is very deep, hard for the mind to fully reach on its own, and needs clear explanation.

questions.question: What does the passage call this truth besides a proof?
questions.answer: It calls it a useful wisdom, a great key, and a deep mystery.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the hidden matter about creation that is being explained?
questions.answer: It describes it as a very secret and hard-to-know puzzle.

questions.question: After speaking about this truth, what does the writer do?
questions.answer: He offers great thanks and praise to Allah.

questions.question: What achievement is credited to the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It is credited with solving, uncovering, and proving this amazing mystery.

questions.question: Does the passage give the full explanation here, or does it point readers to other parts for the full discussion?
questions.answer: It points readers to other parts for the full discussion and only plans a short outline here.

questions.question: Instead of repeating the whole proof here, what does the writer choose to do?
questions.answer: He chooses to give only a short summary of the foundations and proofs.

questions.question: How many mystery-topics does he intend to point to?
questions.answer: Thirteen.

questions.question: What caused the work on the rest to stop?
questions.answer: Strong outer and inner obstacles caused it to stop.

questions.question: What special idea about Allah’s creation is at the center of this passage?
questions.answer: The idea is that the biggest and smallest created things are equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: How is this truth connected to the “word of unity”?
questions.answer: It is presented as part of the meaning and proof of declaring Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What does the passage say this explanation does to the hidden meanings of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It opens them up like a key opening something closed.

questions.question: What does the passage say about philosophy’s ability to solve this issue?
questions.answer: It says philosophy cannot handle or solve it.

questions.question: Who is praised with many thanks in the passage?
questions.answer: Allah, the Compassionate Creator.

questions.question: How certain does the passage say these proofs are?
questions.answer: It says they are as certain as a simple math fact that cannot be denied.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention different sections of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: To show where readers can find fuller explanations of this matter.

questions.question: What does the writer say he will do in this passage instead of giving every detail?
questions.answer: He says he will briefly mention the main bases and proofs.

questions.question: What smaller goal does the writer keep for this passage?
questions.answer: He keeps the smaller goal of briefly laying out the main foundations and proofs.

questions.question: Which of the mysteries had already been written?
questions.answer: The first and second.

questions.question: According to the passage, what truth of faith is being clarified?
questions.answer: The truth that Allah’s oneness is shown in His power to create all things, whether huge or tiny, with no difference in difficulty.

questions.question: What had the writer managed to write from that plan?
questions.answer: He had managed to write the first two.

questions.question: What number of mysteries was planned in the short outline?
questions.answer: Thirteen mysteries.

questions.question: What do the thirteen mysteries seem to represent in the writer’s plan?
questions.answer: They seem to represent a step-by-step outline for explaining the subject.
